recommended_title: Scale-Adaptive Compositional Conformal Regions: Reliability and Limits
central_question: Across the tested synthetic response distributions, dimensions, and covariate regimes, how do training-only scale-adaptive ILR conformal regions trade observed-composition coverage against uniform-simplex region mass relative to matched-center alternatives?
central_thesis: In the six tested synthetic settings, scale-adaptive ILR regions exhibit condition-dependent reliability–efficiency trade-offs rather than uniform dominance: near-target IID coverage coexists with shifted Dirichlet undercoverage, and higher aggregate utility does not imply smaller simplex regions or conditional validity.
narrative_rationale: The strongest evidence is the completed final evaluation with eight seed blocks, paired region constructions, three nominal coverage levels, and explicit coverage, reference-mass, and uncertainty records. It supports a bounded empirical study, not a search-success narrative or a causal claim that rank-based selection improves performance. The IID Dirichlet K=8 comparison and the shifted Dirichlet reversals supply complementary evidence for one thesis. Final qualification is independently recorded as completed/qualified/true; this administrative outcome does not certify scientific generality. No downstream_study is present.
edit_framing_decision: No edit context, previous_paper manuscript, aggregated bundle, or extra_tasks bundle is staged, so there is no prior manuscript to preserve or rewrite. Recentered denotes narrowing the broad source-task motivation and earlier proposed geometry audit to the actually evaluated fixed-ILR scale-adaptation study. Do not imply that an earlier paper was revised.
staged_input_impact: The final evaluator evidence, rather than qualitative memory, sets the main paper scope: logistic-normal IID, Dirichlet IID, and shifted Dirichlet responses, each at K=3 and K=8.

The available selected configuration source implements fixed Helmert ILR ridge centers, bounded local-moment scale correction, and nested training-only rank/ILR-box-volume selection; it does not implement the initially proposed geometry comparison or Mondrian calibration.
The available Gaussian-selector configuration is useful for describing the intervention but has search-plane evidence only; it is not a final-evaluation selector ablation.
Final qualification sources report a completed, qualified evaluation. No failed qualification is present in this run; nevertheless all observed performance limitations remain central.
The supplied ICLR style is single-column with 5.5-inch text width and 9-inch text height. This rules out importing a two-column figure plan.

Bibliography and provenance files now exist, but retrieval metadata alone does not establish that a work has been read or supports a scientific statement. No additional literature search is needed for strategy generation.

method_groups.name: Training-only scale-adaptive ILR regions
method_groups.include_reason: The frozen studied configuration: fixed-basis ridge centers, positive diagonal base scales, shrunk scalar local-moment correction, training-only rank-volume selection, and independent pooled split calibration. Proposed denotes the studied configuration, not proven novelty or superiority of its selector.

method_groups.name: Unscaled ILR regions with matched centers
method_groups.include_reason: Evaluator-owned unit-scale construction retains the studied method's centers and basis, isolating the effect of the complete scaling package relative to no scaling. It does not isolate the local correction or rank selector separately.

method_groups.name: Simplex-coordinate L-infinity regions
method_groups.include_reason: Matched inverse-ILR centers with a jointly calibrated maximum simplex-coordinate residual provide the primary direct comparator; this construction has the largest aggregate utility among the three standard evaluator comparators, but that post-evaluation observation must not be presented as a preregistered selection rule.

method_groups.name: Coordinatewise Bonferroni regions
method_groups.include_reason: Matched simplex centers with coordinatewise finite-rank calibration at alpha/K provide a simultaneous-coordinate comparison. Include in the main summary table and full supplemental comparisons rather than creating a separate narrative.

method_groups.name: Feature-information and degenerate-region controls
method_groups.include_reason: Constant-center, constant-input, and permuted-input results bound interpretations of feature use. Whole-simplex and zero-radius controls check metric endpoints. These are supporting diagnostics, not rival deployable methods or proof of conditional validity.

results_focus: Use only final.evidence.episodes for the principal comparisons: eight seeds, six conditions, and nominal coverage 0.95, 0.90, and 0.80. Present the six conditions as a shared design with condition-specific limits, not successive experiments.

Lead with observed coverage against nominal coverage, separating IID logistic-normal, IID Dirichlet, and shifted Dirichlet settings. The final mean absolute coverage errors are 0.013562011718750005 for IID and 0.13034261067708333 for shift; these are errors, not signed undercoverage rates.

Report a four-method summary table of IID absolute coverage error, shifted absolute coverage error, uniform-simplex mass, and explicitly defined utility. Preserve the equal weighting across seeds, cases, and alpha values; do not pool unequal settings by test-row count.

Show paired utility and simplex-mass differences against the simplex-coordinate comparator for every condition and all three alpha values. The selected method has aggregate utility 0.661819668104677 and a comparator gap of 0.011594669497844157, yet its mean simplex mass is 0.3034934467739529 versus approximately 0.291701 for that comparator. This is not a uniform size improvement or an established significant aggregate advantage.

Explain the matched-center scaling comparison, especially IID Dirichlet K=8, alongside counterexamples: logistic-normal K=3 does not uniformly benefit from scaling, and shifted Dirichlet comparisons against simplex-coordinate regions reverse the aggregate utility ordering.

Distinguish the ILR-box-volume objective used for training-only selection from the uniform-simplex probability mass measured in evaluation. Their different reference measures are factual; a causal account of any observed reversal is not established.

Use the available paired seed bootstrap intervals, marginal Wilson intervals, feature-group records, and Monte Carlo resolution diagnostics at their actual levels. Retain unfavorable comparisons and intervals spanning zero; do not select only favorable nominal coverage levels.

Do not report campaign winner margins, original-incumbent improvements, or scored/unscored attempt counts: downstream_study and study.* grounding entries are absent. Archived alternatives remain search-only context and cannot be mixed with final performance. The original initializer lacks matched final result records and is omitted as a performance comparator, not silently renamed as the unscaled ablation.

figure_specs.layout_rationale: The ICLR text column is the full 5.5-inch text width. A three-part horizontal overview at about 5.39 inches wide and 1.6 inches high allows short labels at 9–10 pt; do not shrink a crowded diagram. Place on page 1 if naturally possible, otherwise page 2, with about 0.30–0.35 page including caption.
figure_specs.content: Training X,Y -> fixed ILR center/base scale -> local-moment correction and nested pseudo-calibration selection; separate calibration Y -> finite-rank threshold -> region for an observed composition; evaluator -> coverage and uniform-simplex probe mass across IID/shift. Put all pseudo-calibration inside the training partition. Use no invented region shapes, numerical measurements, model architectures, or causal arrows from surrogate optimization to empirical gains.
figure_specs.outputs: Preserve editable draw.io source and prompt log. Prefer vector PDF exported from that source when available; otherwise regenerate the overview raster at least 2400 px wide. Never enlarge an existing raster. The later writing/orchestration stage owns generation.

figure_specs.purpose: Expose near-target IID behavior and the shifted Dirichlet coverage deficit without hiding nominal-level dependence in an aggregate error.
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Two panels side by side within the single 5.5-inch ICLR column give roughly 2.5-inch plotting widths. Three target values and three regime curves remain readable with shared axes, 9-pt ticks, a common legend, and a thin identity reference; budget about 0.40–0.45 page with caption. Use the observed data range, explicitly mark any truncated coverage axis, and do not force a zero origin that erases the IID differences.
figure_specs.content: For the frozen scaled-ILR method only, plot target coverage 0.80, 0.90, 0.95 against empirical coverage for logistic-normal IID, Dirichlet IID, and Dirichlet shift. The fourth series budget is reserved for the identity reference. This is a calibration comparison, not a temporal trajectory. Baseline comparisons appear in Figure 3 and the main table.
figure_specs.uncertainty: The writer may derive deterministic 95% seed-block percentile intervals from the eight existing per-seed coverage records, resampling seeds jointly across levels and cases. Such mean-coverage intervals are not already supplied in the stored uncertainty object and must be labeled as a new analysis of existing results. Do not average per-episode Wilson endpoints or treat test rows as eight-seed replicates.
figure_specs.outputs: Save reproducible plot source, vector figures/coverage_by_regime.pdf, and figures/coverage_by_regime.png at 300 DPI; LaTeX must reference the PDF.

figure_specs.purpose: Demonstrate condition-dependent utility and region-mass differences, including the shifted counterexamples to uniform dominance.

figure_specs.split_by: K and metric, arranged as a 2-by-2 grid
figure_specs.layout_rationale: Four compact forest panels need the full single-column text width, not a nominal half-column figure. Rows distinguish dimensions; columns distinguish metrics. Three short regime labels and three target markers fit at 9 pt. Use shared scales within each metric column, a common legend, and zero reference lines; budget about 0.60–0.70 page with caption. If labels collide, shorten labels and increase height within this budget rather than reducing type size.
figure_specs.content: Within each panel show logistic-normal IID, Dirichlet IID, and Dirichlet shift, with separate markers for alpha=0.05, 0.10, 0.20. Utility difference above zero favors scaled ILR; mass difference below zero indicates smaller regions. These signs have different meanings and must be stated separately, never collapsed into a single success rate. Show all levels rather than a favorable subset.
figure_specs.uncertainty: Use each case's paired_baselines.simplex_linf records: utility_difference with paired_seed_bootstrap95 and volume_difference with paired_volume_bootstrap95. Intervals are descriptive 95% seed-bootstrap intervals. Available bonferroni54_bootstrap_interval values apply to utility comparisons only and belong in the supplemental multiplicity table, not as volume uncertainty or exact familywise certificates.
figure_specs.outputs: Save reproducible plot source, vector figures/paired_region_tradeoffs.pdf, and figures/paired_region_tradeoffs.png at 300 DPI; LaTeX must reference the PDF.

Include whole-simplex and zero-radius controls, and distinguish per-context resolution from the average across contexts.

notes_for_writer: Use a thesis-first standalone structure: Introduction; Related Work; Prediction Regions and Evaluation Targets; Training-only Scale Adaptation; Experimental Design and Uncertainty; Reliability–Efficiency Results; Discussion and Limitations; Conclusion. These are scientific sections, not implementation or discovery chronology.

Figure space is already included. Reflow within 8–9 pages without changing template geometry; an eight-page body requires its last page at least 75% full. Spend spare space on equations, paired comparisons, uncertainty interpretation, and limitations, not extra chronology or decorative figures.

The inspected supplied ICLR article template and paper.sty define one 5.5-inch text column and 9-inch text height. Full_width means that same text column, not a two-column float. A half-width inset would be about 2.64 inches at fraction 0.48 and is unsuitable for the required multi-panel figures. Keep 9-pt or larger final-size plot labels and captions consistent with venue style.

Follow VENUE.md: anonymous ICLR 2026 submission, no names, affiliations, acknowledgements, funding, identifying links, or authorship-revealing first-person prior-work references. The supplied template contains a populated author placeholder and final-copy command; do not carry those into an anonymized submission unchanged. Preserve required infrastructure watermark behavior without introducing identifying authorship.

Contributions are a fully specified training-only scale-adaptive configuration, a paired evaluation separating coverage and reference mass, and bounded empirical findings and failure diagnostics. Do not claim a new conformal theorem, comprehensive benchmark, unique new geometry, or causal selector advantage. The existing comparisons do not isolate rank selection from the Gaussian selector in the final plane.

State the score and region explicitly: z=log(y)B, r=max_j |z_j-mu_j(x)|/s_j(x), q from order ceil((n_cal+1)(1-alpha)), and C(x)={positive simplex y:r<=q}. If the rank exceeds n_cal, the calibration threshold is infinite. Training pseudo-calibration has its own documented fallback. The standard split-conformal exchangeability argument is background, conditional on the fitted training-only rule; it is neither a measured guarantee under shift nor a conditional-on-X guarantee.

Describe the correction as a covariate-dependent scalar multiplier shared across ILR coordinates, applied to positive diagonal base scales. The center and base-scale fits are fixed across the local-correction selectors; the evaluator's unscaled ablation instead sets all scales to one. Do not equate these two different controls.

Define reference mass as probability under Dirichlet(1,...,1), averaged over sampled test contexts; it is normalized simplex volume, not ILR-box volume or an absolute Euclidean-volume number. Raw masses at K=3 and K=8 are not directly comparable as intrinsic efficiency rankings. Do not claim exact structural-zero support: responses are positive and the Dirichlet generator applies a declared positivity floor followed by closure.

Define utility U=(1-V) max(0,1-|coverage-(1-alpha)|/(1-alpha)). Its absolute-error penalty includes overcoverage, and a higher U is not itself a coverage-validity certificate. Treat U as a benchmark-specific trade-off summary alongside the separate components, not as the paper's sole result or an externally standardized metric.

Keep key quantitative anchors in the body, including the shifted failures and the selected method's larger aggregate mass than simplex-coordinate L-infinity. All new derived baseline aggregates, confidence intervals, rounding, and tables must be regenerated from the final records by saved analysis code; they are not additional experiments. Do not claim a significant overall utility advantage from the selected method's own score interval.

Final status and qualification must be grounded only in final.qualification.status, final.qualification.outcome, and final.qualification.correct: this run reports completed, qualified, and true. Preserve that outcome without converting it to generalization, conditional validity, or superiority. If later authoritative evidence reports not_qualified, disclose it in writing, review, audit, and revision without attributing the cause unless gate evidence identifies it; missing diagnostics stay unknown.

Preserve final source/result hashes in the audit trail. The archived selected source is linked through the available configuration records and final evidence; do not claim an independently rehashed local final source tree if it has not been recovered and checked.

Private-only grounding context: available identifiers use result.* and final.*, not study.*. Name the frozen evaluated method by its scientific mechanism. Omit campaign winner assertions, search-score margins, and scored/unscored accounting without the required study.* sources; never count missing measurements as losses. Search and final seed sets differ and must not be pooled into a larger replication count or compared as performance improvement over time.

Use eight seeds as the outer repeated unit, not six cases times three alpha levels times eight seeds as independent experiments. Each seed wrapper repeats the same seed_block_uncertainty object; read one copy. For any derived aggregate comparison, resample complete seed blocks jointly across cases, alpha values, and methods. Stored Wilson intervals describe binomial test uncertainty within a fitted episode, not variability over retraining or simultaneous subgroup validity.

Interpret existing paired bootstrap intervals descriptively with only eight seeds. The supplied 54-comparison adjusted utility endpoints are bootstrap percentile endpoints at adjusted tails, not a finite-sample familywise coverage theorem. Do not infer exact significance from them; no adjusted volume interval is supplied.

The shift stress changes test covariates from training uniform support [-1.5,1.5] to clipped normal covariates on [-2.5,3]. It therefore includes support expansion and loss of exchangeability; it does not isolate which mechanism causes undercoverage. The conditional generator is retained, but support mismatch prevents promising that ordinary density-ratio weighting would repair the failures. No weighted-conformal comparator was evaluated.

Keep the main limitations explicit: synthetic responses only, K=3 and K=8 only, fixed ILR basis and region family, pooled rather than subgroup calibration, no exact structural zeros, limited seeds and nominal levels, finite probe resolution, surrogate/reference-measure mismatch, absent final selector-only ablation, and no matched final original-initializer comparison. No CIFAR, classification-label coverage, latent-probability recovery, Hellinger comparison, Mondrian method, or real-data transfer result is supported.

Use condition colors consistently across overview and quantitative panels; encode alpha by marker shape and method by labels or line style rather than reusing a condition color for a different meaning. Do not add trajectory plots: the nominal-level calibration axis is not a search iteration axis.

Quantitative figure source must export both PDF and 300-DPI PNG. Reference PDFs from LaTeX whenever available. Raster-only full-width assets require at least 2400 pixels; any future column-width raster inset requires at least 1200 pixels. Regenerate from source rather than upscaling.
